facts.statement: Callawayasaurus is classified as a genus of plesiosaur within the family Elasmosauridae.
facts.quote: Callawayasaurus is a genus of plesiosaur from the family Elasmosauridae.

facts.statement: The species was originally described by Samuel Paul Welles in 1962 as Alzadasaurus colombiensis and later reclassified into the genus Callawayasaurus by Kenneth Carpenter in 1999.
facts.quote: When the holotype was first described by Samuel Paul Welles in 1962, it was described as Alzadasaurus colombiensis before being moved into its current genus by Kenneth Carpenter in 1999.

facts.statement: The genus name Callawayasaurus honors the paleontologist Jack M. Callaway.
facts.quote: Callawayasaurus is named in honor of the paleontologist Jack M. Callaway

facts.statement: Callawayasaurus was a large plesiosaur with a skull measuring 35 cm and a total body length between 7.4 and 8 meters.
facts.quote: Callawayasaurus was a large plesiosaur, with a skull length of 35 cm and body length of 7.4 - 8 m.

facts.statement: Callawayasaurus possessed elongated nares positioned over the maxilla, which contained between 3 and 5 teeth.
facts.quote: The nares of Callawayasaurus are elongated and positioned over the maxilla, which has 3-5 teeth.

facts.statement: The neck of Callawayasaurus contained 56 vertebrae, which were relatively short compared to other elasmosaurids.
facts.quote: The neck contains 56 vertebrae which are relatively short compared to other elasmosaurids.

facts.statement: Fossils of Callawayasaurus lack pectoral bars, a structure found in other plesiosaur species.
facts.quote: Callawayasaurus fossils have no pectoral bars

facts.statement: A nearly complete skeleton found to be more robust than the holotype suggests that Callawayasaurus may have exhibited sexual dimorphism.
facts.quote: Another nearly complete skeleton was found to be slightly more robust than the holotype specimen. This subtle change may indicate sexual dimorphism.

facts.statement: Callawayasaurus lived during the Aptian stage of the Early Cretaceous period, approximately 125 to 112 million years ago.
facts.quote: Callawayasaurus are known from the Aptian faunal stage of the early Cretaceous period, which extended from 125 to 112 million years ago.

facts.statement: The first remains of Callawayasaurus were discovered in the Paja Formation near Leiva, Boyaca, Colombia.
facts.quote: The first Callawayasaurus remains were found in the Paja Formation near Leiva, Boyaca Colombia.

facts.statement: Callawayasaurus originated from the Aptian stage during the Early Cretaceous period, spanning from 125 to 112 million years ago.
facts.quote: Callawayasaurus procede del Aptiense durante el periodo Cretácico Inferior, el cual comprendió desde hace 125 hasta 112 millones de años.

rejected.statement: The specific time range for Callawayasaurus is estimated to be between 121.4 and 119.57 million years ago.
rejected.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 119.57 million years ago)
